instruction: As a sports commentator, describe the winning play in the final seconds of a championship game.
response:
The winning play in a championship game is often one that sets up the ultimate victory. It could be a decisive shot, a penalty kick or even a goal from the opposing team's goalkeeper. The key to this play is to execute it flawlessly and with precision. The ball must be hit just right at the moment when the opposing team has no time to react, allowing the home team to take control of the match. 

For example, if the home team is playing against the defending champion, they may have a few minutes left on the clock before the final whistle blows. In such a situation, the home team can make a quick pass to their striker who will then score the winning goal. This play not only sets up the final moments but also gives the home team an edge over the opposition. 

In conclusion, the winning play is crucial in determining the outcome of a championship match. A well-executed play can set the stage for a great result and give the home team a chance to claim the trophy.
